Executive Principal's Welcome
Welcome to Haberdashers' Crayford Academy, a vibrant and inclusive school community where every student is encouraged to thrive, and every family is warmly welcomed.
Whether you’re joining us in Year 7, entering another year group, or stepping into our Sixth Form for the first time, we’re excited to have you become part of our school family.
At Crayford Academy, we proudly offer a rich educational experience, combining academic excellence with a deep commitment to character development. From our youngest pupils in our own Trust Primary schools at age 3, through to those preparing to step into the world beyond school, we are here to support and guide you at every stage of your journey. Our motto, "aged 3 to forever," reflects our belief that the learning and values you gain here will stay with you throughout your life, shaping your future in profound and lasting ways.
Many of our new students have already experienced life within our Trust through one of our primary schools, while others are drawn to us from across the local area, inspired by our strong ethos and outstanding reputation. No matter where you come from, you will find a home here.
Our school may be larger than average, but our approach to education is deeply personal. We believe in getting to know each student and their family, working in partnership to achieve the best possible outcomes—both academically and personally. From your very first day with us, you’ll find that our expectations are high, and our support is unwavering. Our dedicated team of Pastoral & Wellbeing Mentors are here to help you settle in, offering guidance and strategies to ensure a smooth transition, no matter which year group you’re joining.
The ‘Haberdashers’ Advantage’ is a hallmark of our Trust, providing unique opportunities for all our students. We work closely with the Haberdashers’ Company, whose members often mentor our students, sharing their wealth of knowledge and experience. These connections open doors to future pathways, including Apprenticeships and other career opportunities. Our school’s strong emphasis on essential literacy and numeracy skills underpins our broad curriculum, ensuring that every student is well-prepared for the challenges and opportunities that lie ahead.
We are particularly proud of our thriving Sixth Form, where students not only excel in their studies but also serve as role models for the entire school. They help promote the values and ethos that define our community, setting the standard for behaviour, uniform, and conduct.
Our facilities are second to none, purpose-built to support a wide range of abilities and interests. Whether you’re passionate about academics, sports, the arts, or extracurricular activities, you’ll find that our environment is designed to help you succeed. We are a school where students feel safe, supported, and inspired to achieve their very best.
Haberdashers’ Crayford Academy is a place where stability, self-esteem, and a sense of belonging flourish. With over 1,000 pupils, we are a vibrant and dynamic community that is deeply committed to making a positive difference in the local area. As Executive Principal, I am determined that our school, staff, and students continue to contribute meaningfully to the community we serve.
We are incredibly proud to be Haberdashers’ Crayford Academy, where we truly believe in shaping your future—starting at age 3 and continuing forever. We can’t wait to welcome you—whether you’re a prospective student, a new family, or a visitor—to experience all that our school has to offer. Come and be part of something truly special.
Together, Stronger

Welcome
Schools within the Haberdashers’ Academies Trust South have provided excellent Sixth Form opportunities for well over a hundred years. The Sixth Form at Crayford Academy was established in September 2015 and builds upon this strong record with an ethos and expectations of high academic outcomes. Our Sixth Form fosters a culture of community and belonging. All of our young people have responsibility and purpose whilst they study at Crayford, through several roles offered to them including The Youth Advisory Board, reading buddies, prefects and the charity team. Also, our pupils have a world of opportunities at their fingertips through our unique character curriculum: The Haberdashers' Advantage. ​ It is with thanks to our staff, the Worshipful Company of Haberdashers, our community, and our many partners, that the Haberdashers' experience for every pupil is like no other. By giving them this advantage, we support our pupils to be happy, confident and successful individuals who will contribute to making their communities – and the world – a better place. Our Sixth Form community thrive from Careers Events, The Haberdashers' Aspire Mentoring Programme, The Livery Awards and The Haberdashers Wilderness Foundation to name but a few.
Haberdashers' Crayford Sixth Form offers the opportunity for young people to study, socialise and develop in a structured and caring environment.
Our students make excellent progress in their studies and become well rounded individuals ready for their next steps in Higher Education, apprenticeships or employment.
We are a highly popular Sixth Form with a thriving community of approximately 130 students who make a significant contribution to school life.
Enrichment in the sixth form
Our enrichment programme is varied with students able to choose form a wide range of activities: the Extended Project qualification, which is an excellent preparation for university studies and well-regarded by admissions tutors, Core Maths, The Duke of Edinburgh Scheme, our sports and fitness programme, music lessons, the Debating Society and many others. Our students also take part in a range of national competitions, which gives them access to high-calibre mentoring, coaching and networking experiences. We have fantastic links with the EY Foundation, where successful candidates complete a 12-month programme giving our young people the opportunity to gain paid work experience and take part in interactive employability skills workshops during the school holidays. They are also offered the opportunity to network with both employers and other young people, as well as having access to their own supportive mentor to help guide them into the first stage of a career or higher education.
Leadership in the Sixth Form
A key strategy we use to ensure our students can fulfil their personal and academic aspirations is through providing a wide range of opportunities. Student leadership is a key priority and we ensure that all sixth formers have the chance to fulfil a leadership role via our Head Boy and Head Girl Team, becoming a Prefect, Peer Mentoring younger students, charity drives, and by representing the school on a local and even national scale. Our students are fortunate to have the full support and backing of the Worshipful Company of Haberdashers, giving them a distinct advantage that other Sixth Forms cannot offer.
Destinations
Our Destination pathways are bespoke and cater for a wide range of aspirations; we support students in year 13 to secure places at University, and we work with numerous guest speakers and apprenticeship providers to support students who want to enter the world of employment, apprenticeships and training. Indeed, many of these claim places on highly sought after A-Level leaver programmes.
Ultimately, teaching and learning is our core business and we are proud to boast a high quality of provision across our curriculum which truly distinguishes our Sixth Form. We are proud of the success academically and personally of the young men and women who, when they leave our Sixth Form, are in a far stronger position to make a success of their lives and contribute to the world in which they live.

Enrichment
The Crayford Committment
Personal development sits at the heart of our vision for excellence, opportunity, and belonging at Haberdashers' Crayford Academy. Our curriculum is built around four core values — Community, Critical Thinking, Confidence, and Courage — which together shape our Personal Development offer. Through this framework, we ensure that every pupil, regardless of background or starting point, experiences a rich programme of PSHE, enrichment, leadership, trips, and wider opportunities that build cultural capital and open doors that may otherwise be closed. Our approach is rooted in a strong belief in social mobility: education should broaden horizons, remove barriers, and empower every young person to shape their own future.
Our intent is simple: every pupil will leave us as a confident, thoughtful, and courageous young person — equipped with the knowledge, character, and ambition to thrive academically, socially, and personally in a rapidly changing world, and to contribute positively to their community.
Personal Development Curriculum Intent
We prioritise the physical, emotional, and mental wellbeing of all secondary pupils, ensuring they feel safe, supported, and able to thrive. Through PSHE, RSE, pastoral systems, safeguarding education, and open dialogue, pupils learn how to make informed choices, build healthy relationships, and keep themselves and others safe both online and offline.
Leadership roles and enrichment opportunities—including Hub events, cultural experiences, and wider partnerships—enable pupils to contribute meaningfully and understand the world beyond their community.
Enrichment and experiences strengthen this sense of community. Pupils take part in Hub activities, cultural events, visiting speakers, and community-focused projects, building pride in diversity and shared identity. Opportunities linked to the wider Haberdashers’ network and Advantage, including enrichment experiences and partnerships and, broaden pupils’ understanding of the world beyond Crayford.
We develop pupils who can think deeply, question constructively, and engage critically with the world around them. Through PSHE, RSE, assemblies, and curriculum enrichment, pupils explore democracy, justice, rights, and responsibilities, learning to evaluate information and challenge bias.
Across subjects, scholarship and literacy development foster analytical thinking, intellectual curiosity, and the ability to form and justify reasoned arguments. Pupils are encouraged to become reflective learners who can engage confidently in respectful, evidence-based discussion.
This is strengthened through enrichment opportunities including debating activities, academic lectures, STEM experiences, and subject-based visits, helping pupils apply knowledge beyond the classroom and think like scholars.
Raising aspirations is central to our secondary provision. Our careers programme ensures pupils are ambitious, informed, and prepared for next steps into further education, apprenticeships, or employment. Pupils benefit from structured guidance, employer engagement, and access to platforms such as Unifrog to support goal setting and reflection.
A wide range of experiences builds confidence in and beyond the classroom. Pupils engage in university and employer encounters, careers fairs and workshops, alongside exposure to enrichment opportunities and external speakers linked to industry and higher education.
Enrichment experiences further broaden confidence and cultural capital, including UCAS-style awareness events, STEM opportunities, leadership programmes, and wider curriculum enrichment days and trips, ensuring pupils see and experience ambitious futures as achievable.
We explicitly develop courage in pupils to make positive choices, embrace challenge, and step beyond their comfort zones. This includes the courage to speak up, take responsibility, and act with integrity in all aspects of school life.
Through our curriculum, pupils are encouraged to take intellectual risks, participate in debate, and persevere through academic challenge. Resilience is built through structured support and high expectations, helping pupils to see setbacks as part of growth.
Courage is also developed through our PSHE education, where pupils learn to recognise risk, seek help, and make safe decisions in complex situations. This is extended through enrichment opportunities such as trips, visits, leadership roles, and participation in wider academy experiences, helping pupils develop independence, adaptability, and confidence.

Learning Resources Centre
Welcome to the Crayford Learning Resource Centre
Visit the LRC to explore and discover what we have to offer!
You will receive a warm welcome and find plenty of great resources. Choose from the extensive range of books, browse the magazines and daily newspapers, sit on a sofa or beanbag and read, use a computer or Ipad, take an AR quiz, look at careers and university information, borrow a DVD, or complete independent study assignments. We are open before and after school every day for study, reading, research and relaxation and look forward to seeing you!

Trips and Visits
Educational Visits
Educational Visits normally take place during the school day but a number involve an overnight stay of at least one night.
Full details of the arrangements for travel, activities involved and the cost will be given to parents well in advance of the proposed visit.
Information about the visits will be sent to parents in advance. Parent consent for students to attend, and payment where required, must be received in advance and by the deadline set by the school. Students will be unable to attend if the consent is not received. Consent is obtained via the Arbor Parent App or Portal.
Educational Visits may involve travel abroad (e.g. Foreign Languages, Battlefields, leisure activities). Parents are reminded that they are responsible for ensuring that their child has the correct documentation for such a trip (e.g. valid passport). Parents should also note that the Academy insurance cover is limited to travel, life and medical costs only and does not cover the repair / replacement of personal effects (e.g. mobile phones, MP3 players). Additional insurance to cover the cost of these items is the responsibility of parents.
Some educational visits are an integral part of the Academy curriculum and as such are compulsory.
Day trips will usually start and end at the Academy and students will be required to wear full school uniform.
Payments for some visits may be spread over a period of time and should be made through the ParentPay account. Please note that grants are available to help with payment, for students who are eligible for free school meals.
If you have not yet activated your ParentPay account and require some guidance to do this, please use the link below.
https://support.parentpaygroup.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4409658059153-Payer-guidance-How-to-activate-your-account
Login details were sent for new students during the Summer break, however if you no longer have these please contact the school and we can resend them to you.

Careers and Employability
Enabling our students to achieve their full potential
“Careers education is about inspiration and aspiration as much as advice.”
At Crayford Academy we believe a good quality Careers Education Information, Advice and Guidance (CEIAG) programme increases the aspirations and achievement of every student and supports our core vision, “Learning Changes Lives”.
Our Careers Vision
The vision of our careers coordinator is that students will leave our school with the drive and ambition to accomplish their chosen career pathway, and that they will become ambitious, successful, caring citizens equipped with the confidence and skills capable of making decisions in any given situation.
That is why, in addition to the wealth of early support students receive each year, we offer independent careers interviews from an early age, as well as having a dedicated careers lead.
Having a careers lead within the school means that pupils have instant access to a number of careers services throughout the school day, this will ensure that our pupils are well informed and able to take advantage of the array of opportunities available to them. Our main focus being on supporting our pupils long-term careers ambitions, making use of our exceptionally trained tutors, utilising our links with external consultants and speakers from some of the UK’s largest companies. In addition to our careers lead our students follow an extensive careers program, this prepares them for making informed decisions about their future, applications for university, apprenticeships, college or work; whichever is their chosen pathway.
The Careers provision is guided and evaluated against the Gatsby Benchmarks, which we are proud to meet each one. Career exploration, experience of industry and application support are key to enriching the post-16 offer and ensuring our students are prepared for their next stage of education, higher apprenticeships or employment.
For Further information, please contact our careers Co-ordinator, Mrs L Dodd-Teis | l.dodd-teis@habstrustsouth.org.uk | 01322402180
Date of Next Review of the published Information: September 2026
How can our parents/carers support our careers programme?
We recognise that parents/carers come from many different work backgrounds and can also contribute to helping our students make informed decisions. Therefore, if you are able to offer some time to deliver an occupational talk, host a stand at our annual careers fair, or are able to take a student for a work experience placement we would eagerly welcome you contacting:
Mrs L Dodd-Teis l.dodd-teis@habstrustsouth.org.uk
How do we prepare students for the future?
Crayford Academy understands that all students need to prepare themselves for progression through learning and education into adulthood. We aim to prepare students for life after school by providing information on the ever-changing future occupations and progression routes to sixth form, college, university or work/apprenticeships.
We are committed to providing a varied programme of activities for all students from Year 7 to Year 13 and beyond. Various careers-related opportunities are provided via a number of different methods such as:
The academy utilises the expertise of the Crayford Academy Careers Coordinator who supports students on a regular basis. Students also have the opportunity to book a personal appointment with the Crayford Academy Careers Coordinator by emailing l.dodd-teis@habstrustsouth.org.uk . These sessions can be 1-2-1 or completed in a group.
We offer particular support for SEND students. The aim is to provide activities and events that meet the needs of the individual students. We offer independent and impartial careers guidance to support career and option choices, raising the aspirations of individual students and equipping them with the necessary skills, attitudes, knowledge and understanding.

THE IMPORTANCE OF DESTINATION MEASURES
Careers Information, Advice and Guidance is a key part of our student offer, we provide a comprehensive and personalised programme of support throughout KS4 and KS5 to help students secure both a suitable and sustainable destination. The Careers and Employability Service supports academic learning and delivers impact through a variety of interventions such as talks, work experience, mentoring, competitions and general advice. One of the ways we can really assess impact is by looking at our destinations data.
The majority of Post 16 students at Haberdashers' Crayford Academy go on to Sixth Form, Apprenticeship or Further Education College and then University, a Gap Year, Employment or Apprenticeship. All students receive support from specialist staff, we are committed to ensuring that students transition onto suitable and sustainable destinations, our student are consistently being offered a large number of Russell Group places and on a yearly basis we see our students take up the best apprenticeships and school leaver opportunities in the country.

The Haberdashers' Pupil Experience
At Haberdashers' Academies Trust South, we believe in providing a comprehensive education that spans from early childhood to post -16 study. We understand that it takes time and consistency to nurture children and young people into individuals with strong character.
Our schools embrace the unique diversities of their local areas in and around south east London. We are committed to ensuring that all our students thrive, regardless of their background or future aspirations. We believe it is crucial for them to have enriching experiences both inside and outside the classroom, which open doors and broaden their horizons.
We strive to create a seamless transition between different stages of education, ensuring that primary pupils have guaranteed places in our secondary schools (applications must still be made via the local authority).
The curriculum across our schools is designed to cultivate a sense of community and global citizenship in our pupils. We aim to prepare them for an ever-changing future by providing a well-rounded education, equipping them with the necessary tools, opportunities and self-assurance to achieve their full potential.
Haberdashers' Advantage
The Haberdashers' Advantage programme is a unique offering in our schools. It empowers our children and young people to focus on their skills, talents, and abilities, fostering a positive mindset and enabling them to make meaningful contributions to their communities and the world.
From primary school to sixth form, all Haberdashers' students have the chance to participate in character-building experiences that help shape their futures. These opportunities are made possible through partnerships with the Worshipful Company of Haberdashers and other key organisations.
The programme revolves around three core areas: student leadership, futures, and community action. Through this comprehensive approach, our pupils gain the confidence, knowledge, and ambition to strive for their individual future paths.
Learn more about the Haberdashers' Advantage
Our Curriculum
When we plan our curriculum, we think of the child's whole journey through school from 3 to 18. Our approach is based on establishing strong learning foundations from the Early Years stage so that every child is rooted in key skills and knowledge from the outset.
This provides building blocks for every child's learning journey helping them to make connections in their knowledge. Our curriculum follows statutory guidance but offers a global outlook that reflects the rich diversity of our school communities that is guided by the Haberdashers' Primary Teaching Principles and Secondary Teaching Principles and Curriculum Experience Model. Our results open doors to many post-school opportunities from apprenticeships to university.
Learn more about our Curriculum on our School Improvement Strategy page
Belong to a Lifelong Network
Being part of the Haberdashers' family means our pupils have access to an unrivalled network of industry leaders, providing unique opportunities.
We are proud of the achievements of our alumni, many of whom choose to give their time and energy back to their schools by inspiring children with their own stories of success; choosing to teach or lead in our schools; or by supporting school leaders in governor roles.
Learn more about our sponsors and the Haberdashers' family

What qualifications can be gained?
The qualification that the students get would is an Edexcel GCSE in French or Spanish 9-1.
How does Modern Foreign Languages prepare students for the next stage of their education or employment?
Bilingual individuals often have access to higher-paying jobs and may receive better compensation than their monolingual counterparts. Language skills can open opportunities for work in different countries or regions, enhancing career mobility and advancement prospects. Learning a new language involves practicing listening, speaking, reading, and writing, which can enhance overall communication skills. The process of language learning requires adapting to new rules and structures, which can make individuals more adaptable and flexible in various situations.
Cultural Awareness and global perspective: Language learning often involves understanding the culture associated with that language, fostering greater empathy and appreciation for diversity. Being able to communicate in another language can broaden a student’s worldview, making them more adaptable and open-minded in a globalized world. Communication skills: Learning a second language forces students to analyze sentence structure, grammar, and syntax. This meta-linguistic awareness directly improves writing, vocabulary, and articulacy in native English. Multilingual students demonstrate superior active listening skills, greater attention to detail, and a heightened ability to decode complex information and read non-verbal cues.
Resilience and Problem-Solving: Navigating a new language builds academic resilience, confidence, and the ability to think logically under pressure - traits highly valued by both higher education institutions and future employers.
